A Leading Independent School in Tonbridge
Hilden Grange Preparatory School
Exceptional Prep Education in Tonbridge
Hilden Grange School is a private independent school in Tonbridge, offering education to children from ages 3-13. One of the leading preparatory schools in Kent, we enable children to set high standards, work hard and realise their true potential in the classroom, onstage and on the sports field.
Our students are academically ambitious. At Hilden Grange, we nurture their ambition and promote excellence with unrivalled academic provision. Specialist teaching and a tailored curriculum deliver top academic results and a path to prestigious secondary schools and grammar schools in our area. Opportunities for growth and development extend far beyond traditional academics: children take part in extensive extracurriculars, fostering valuable skills for school and life beyond.
Hilden Grange offers a supportive, stimulating school experience for boys and girls from rising 3s up to age 13. Our learners develop the tools to excel both in secondary school and, later, university, such as leadership, discipline and a growth mindset. We look forward to welcoming you!
Why Choose Our School in Tonbridge?
At our prep school in Tonbridge, top-tier academic provision is ensured by skilled educators with outstanding qualifications. Pupils in Year 3 onwards enjoy specialist teaching, which elevates lessons and inspires a love of learning. Our academic results are among the best in Kent: not only do our learners excel in their 11+ entrance exams, but a large number secure scholarships to attend a range of top secondary schools.
A long list of destination schools speaks to our record of delivering personalised guidance and preparation: at our prep school in Tonbridge, learners are fully supported in identifying and securing a place at the grammar or secondary school most suited to their needs and interests.
Our exemplary extracurricular programme features 40+ clubs and activities aimed at fostering learners’ unique talents. From elite team and solo sports to the creative and performing arts, we offer numerous opportunities to discover, nurture and explore one’s interests while cultivating in-demand skills and personal qualities.
Subject Specialists from Year 3
Talented teachers promote excellence and offer a challenging, stimulating learning experience.
40+ Extracurricular Activities
Children are empowered to unleash their potential through extensive, expert-led extracurriculars, spanning sports, the arts and other areas.
Academic Achievements
Over the past four years, our pupils at 11+ secured Grammar School places through an impressive 92% to 100% pass rate.
Our learners have received 114 scholarships to prestigious grammar and secondary schools since 2019.
A Wide Selection of Destination Schools
In the last 5 years, we helped children secure places at 30+ secondary schools, catering to pupils’ abilities and interests.

Hilden Grange School is part of Inspired Education. A community of schools spanning six continents, Inspired leads the way in delivering top-tier private education for ages 1 to 18 years. United by a commitment to exceptional standards, Inspired schools offer a holistic approach to learning that combines Academics, Sport, and the Performing and Creative Arts – known collectively as the Pillars of an Inspired Education.
Learn More About Inspired
A Global Group of Premium Schools
A Global Group of Premium Schools
Access to the Inspired community gives your child the best start to their education possible. Our prep school in Tonbridge aims to deliver top-tier education provision based on Inspired’s commitment to fostering tomorrow’s leaders. In addition to up-to-date knowledge and the most innovative resources, learners are pushed to develop their talents outside the classroom too, through expert-led extracurriculars and a wealth of premium learning facilities.
Guaranteed Entry to Inspired Boarding Schools
Guaranteed Entry to Inspired Boarding Schools
Inspired learners are automatically accepted into any of the Group’s premium boarding schools at the secondary school level. With campuses the world over – from Europe to the UK, Kenya to Vietnam – Inspired sets the standard in high-quality boarding provision, with excellent pastoral support, modern facilities, 24-hour care and more.
Hand-Picked Teachers from Around the World
Hand-Picked Teachers from Around the World
Every teacher in the Inspired group has been hand-selected for their values and commitment to outstanding academic provision. From sports coaches to subject specialists, our staff bring top credentials, blending innovative methods and global best practices to promote excellence, inspire curiosity and instil a lifelong love of learning.
Expansive International Experiences
Expansive International Experiences
Hilden Grange, an Inspired school in Tonbridge, benefits from global connectivity with 110+ premium private schools across Europe, Africa, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific and Latin and South America. Our learners embark on transformative experiences that allow them to travel and gain skills for life, whether at specialist summer camps or on exchange programmes overseas.
Discover our leading school in Tonbridge, Kent, where learners unleash their full potential with outstanding academic provision, extensive extracurriculars and a path to prestigious grammar and secondary schools.

Wraparound Care
Stimulating After-School Care for Flexible Schedules
We provide wraparound care from 7:30am to 6pm. In addition to offering a secure environment for learners outside of regular school hours, this programme is carefully planned, with exciting and thrilling experiences to inspire and stimulate learners’ interests. A variety of clubs and activities are available after school, from sports to the arts and cultural opportunities. Our exemplary wraparound care allows learners to pursue their unique ambitions while giving busy parents peace of mind.
Activities and Clubs
With extensive and thrilling activities to choose from, our pupils are encouraged, nurtured and stimulated as they seek to expand and deepen learning outside of the core curriculum. We have clubs for all interests, be they cultural, athletic or artistic. Below is a sample of these clubs which, by providing a holistic education, equips students with the tools to succeed in the 21st century.
Additional wraparound care is available during holidays, in the form our Holiday Club. Any pupil can attend Holiday Club from 9am to 4pm for one week in April and December and three weeks in the Summer holidays.

Inspection Reports
Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) Report February 2025 on Hilden Grange
Hilden Grange was inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate in February 2025 and the school was found to be fully compliant in respect of all regulations and meets all the Independent Schools Standards in the regulatory compliance element of the inspection. These standards address:
Reports no longer provide a formal classification in terms of ‘Excellent, Good, Satisfactory, etc.’ as for last time, and are less descriptive than before. We are, however, delighted at the many positive comments throughout and with the endorsement of the high quality of education provided at Hilden Grange. This is much deserved, given the hard work of the staff, pupils and parents in our school community and we can be justifiably proud of our school and all those associated with Hilden Grange. There are many very positive comments, such as those below, that reflect well on our school:
"The curriculum facilitates the development of skills over time, from the firm foundations built in the early years to the high achievements of pupils in their entrance examinations to senior schools."
"Pupils behave well at school. The ‘Hilden Grange Way’ is an effective framework of statements… that leaders and staff use to promote positive and appropriate behaviour by pupils. It is well understood by pupils and helps them to show kindness and respect towards each other."
"Leaders prioritise pupils’ wellbeing and treat it as a crucial factor that underpins academic success. They create an environment in which kindness and consideration is prominent…"
"Leaders foster an inclusive environment by promoting the principle that diversity should be celebrated and that all individuals are valued."
Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) Report March 2022 on Hilden Grange
Hilden Grange was inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate in March 2022, and we are proud to announce that the school was graded as ‘excellent’, the highest grade possible, in the two areas covered by the report: ‘The Quality of Pupils’ Academic and other Achievements’ and ‘The Quality of Pupil’s Personal Development.’
Malcolm Gough, Headteacher, commented:
“I am delighted that the school has been recognised in this way as it is an endorsement of the high quality of education provided at Hilden Grange and the hard work, dedication and commitment of staff, children and parents. As a community we can be justifiably proud of our school and all those associated with Hilden Grange.”
The inspectors noted that “pupils’ exemplary attitudes were supported by creative and engaging teaching which enables them to become highly effective learners” and added “pupils of all ages are engaged and enthusiastic during lessons; they settle down to studies quickly and work independently and with diligence.”
The report recognizes the firm foundation that children receive in the Early Years and how this is developed through their time at the school:
“A large majority of the youngest children receive a very high level of development by the time they leave the early years setting. As pupils move up the school they maintain this strong start and make rapid progress with standardized test scores in English and mathematics being well above national age-related norms.”
“High level skills in the core subjects are established in the EYFS and, as pupils progress through the school, they develop a well-developed fund of knowledge. This is a result of specialist teaching provided in all subjects from Year 3 upwards.”
Opportunities outside of the curriculum were praised:
“Pupils flourish beyond the classroom in sports, music and the arts. Sports teams achieve highly in inter-school matches in rugby, cricket and athletics. Excellent musicality is promoted through individual instrumental lessons, choirs and music ensembles ranging from Year 1 ocarinas to senior wind band.”
In terms of the pupils’ personal development, the Inspectors wrote that “Pupils show a highly developed sense of moral responsibility supported wholly by the Hilden Grange way of conduct.” They also commented that, “Pupils show high levels of respect and consideration for each other and form productive relationships.”
We were pleased to note that the impact made by our Language of Learning has been recognized:
“Pupils exhibit strong positivity which is nurtured through the six aims of the school’s Language of Learning. This is an everyday common focus for pupils and staff which is embedded within the culture of the school.”
The school was also found to be fully compliant in respect of all regulations in the Regulatory Compliance element of the inspection.

Personalised Tours
Discover Our School First-Hand
We strongly advise parents who are considering Hilden Grange for their child to arrange a personalised tour of our school. Personalised tours let you see and experience the school in person, discover our outstanding facilities and meet some of our dedicated teachers. Prospective parents will learn all all about our exceptional offering and how pupils are nurtured to unleash their full potential.
Our tours take place on weekdays at 9am, or at a time and date suitable for parents. The Headteacher, Mrs Hoffmann, will be happy to discuss any questions or concerns. Kindly complete the form below to arrange your personalised tour.

Nsouli Scholars
A Transformative Opportunity
The Nsouli Scholars Programme is an exciting global initiative that promises to transform lives by enabling 50 extraordinary students at any one time to attend any of Inspired’s prestigious schools on a full scholarship for the duration of their education. The ambition is that the scholarship will provide hundreds of children with an opportunity to receive a truly transformative education.
By opening this path to exceptional individuals, we hope to expand our community, and to empower children of all backgrounds with unrivalled opportunities in academics, sports, the arts and extracurricular activities. In this sense, the Nsouli Scholars Programme is an investment both in education and in shaping the leaders of tomorrow.
This generous endowment honours Nadim Nsouli, who founded Inspired in 2013 as a definitive statement of excellence in private international education. In recognition of Mr Nsouli’s Lebanese heritage and Inspired’s commitment to inclusivity, several scholarships will be awarded to individuals of Lebanese origin.
Learn More Scholarship Award List
Inspired schools offer a world-class educational experience that combines academics and engaging extra-curricular activities, producing confident, multi-skilled students who flourish in a competitive and increasingly interconnected world. Along with expert instruction by hand-picked teachers, our students access specialist sports programmes and professional tutelage from leaders in the performing and creative arts. As a result, they leave armed with a robust value system and a love of learning that extends well beyond the classroom.
Inspired is also committed to leveraging new and transformative learning technologies. Inspired AI empowers children to achieve academic excellence by delivering actionable insights that are unique to each student, including strengths and weaknesses. Our partnership with The Royal College of Music and Forte, a revolutionary online platform, enables children to receive personalised music tuition from professionals. Students with musical interests benefit from bespoke private lessons, advancing their practice as creatives and gaining valuable performance experience.
The advantages of our holistic approach to education are evidenced by the fact that Inspired students consistently excel in academic performance, surpassing national and global averages. In 2022, the Average Point Score was 35 for those undertaking the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma, for which the world average was 31.98, while A* scores comprised 27% of our students' A Level grades, compared to 14.6% globally. As a consequence, many are able to attend leading universities, with one in three graduates going on to a Russell Group University or Ivy League College.
The Inspired Group includes top-rated day and boarding schools worldwide, meaning students enjoy access to a diverse international community. Be it through specialised Summer Camps or immersive Global Exchange Programmes, children have the chance to travel broadly and engage meaningfully with different cultures, meet and learn from our esteemed partners, build lifelong networks, and become more independent.
Discover how an Inspired Scholarship can empower your child with a transformative education, widely-recognised qualifications, and the competencies they need to thrive in an evolving world.

Economic Wellbeing Lessons at Hilden Grange
Our Economic Wellbeing lessons are in full swing as we get ready for our exciting Charity Fair next week! The children have been exploring some big questions about money — why we need it, what it can buy, and how we make thoughtful choices with it.
Through discussions and practical activities, the pupils are discovering the difference between needs and wants, learning how money is earned and saved, and beginning to understand how budgeting works. These lessons are helping them to prepare for the Charity Fair, where they will be putting their new skills into action as they plan, create, and run their own stalls.
It’s wonderful to see their enthusiasm as they develop teamwork, creativity, and a real sense of social responsibility. We’re looking forward to a fantastic event next week!

pageCache.pageTitle: News about our breaktime snacks and lunches! | Hilden Grange
pageCache.text:
News about our breaktime snacks and lunches!
Continually making improvements for our pupils at lunchtime
Following our pupil survey, a group of 32 Year 6, 7 and 8 pupils met with Thomas Franks’ representative, Joby Dawson, Operations Manager and Mrs Patrica Wild, our Thomas Franks local School Catering Manager.
The children’s responses highlighted two main areas for discussion: healthy eating, including snacks for breaktimes, and portion sizes.
Joby and Mrs Wild shared some amazing facts about the food regulations and checks that our school menus go through, and we are delighted to share that, across the group, our menus are exemplary and consistently pass the nutritional check.
As a result of the meeting, we have agreed that pupils will be allowed to have a second helping of the hot main meal and the main pudding option is sufficient. After Easter, yoghurt, an additional pudding offering, will be increased.
The children unanimously agreed that they would like to improve what they eat at breaktimes and reduce crisps and sugary snacks being allowed in school. With some excellent suggestions, we are working to consider a trial, during our Science Week and Mental Health Week next term. Watch this space!
Joby, Mrs Wild and the staff were very impressed with the questions, statements and conversation that the children brought to the hour-long session and, as one of the only schools that brings all stakeholders together, we have certainly given Thomas Franks some ‘food for thought’ with their other schools!

Pastoral Care and SEND
A Nurturing Environment to Support Growth
We are incredibly proud to provide high-quality pastoral care in which learners develop the skills and tools they need to negotiate the challenges of real life. While recognising the uniqueness of each learner, our staff ensure pupils feel safe, happy and integral to the school community, and empower them to reach their full potential. By working collaboratively with our pupils, staff and parents, we build strong relationships and maintain high standards, ensuring all needs are identified and our pupils supported appropriately, be it through peer mentors or scheduled time with our school counsellor.
"Pupils show high levels of respect and consideration for each other and form productive relationships."
ISI Inspection Report
SEND Provision - Mrs Rebekah Sievewright
Head of Learning Support
At Hilden Grange, our specialist subject teaching and setting for Maths and English from Year 3 enable us to cater for each pupil’s individual needs.
When ‘Quality First Teaching’ is insufficient to meet the whole remit of a pupil’s needs, we are proactive in providing early intervention. We actively encourage the involvement of staff, pupils and parents in the education of children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). Learning difficulties such as dyslexia and dyscalculia are assessed and provided for in a variety of ways, so that children have the opportunity to develop to their full potential with the guidance and support of all their teachers.
Provision is made when the children need it, but they are not necessarily defined for life by this provision. Support for bi- and multi-lingual learners, where necessary, is covered under the Learning Support Department umbrella.
Our collaborative approach to pastoral care fosters the skills for success, both in school and life beyond. If you have a question or concern, please let us know by filling in an Enquiry Form.

Our Curriculum
Introducing the Language of Learning
The Language of Learning is a key part of the Hilden Grange ethos, embodied by our broad and balanced curriculum. This approach is used inside and outside the classroom and is based on 6 key traits: challenge, perseverance, confidence, responsibility, positivity and communication.
Students are assessed throughout the year in all subjects and and undergo standardised testing once a year, allowing us to monitor their progress. Our parents receive a full report and we regularly hold parent consultation evenings throughout the academic year.
Pupils exhibit strong positivity which is nurtured through the six aims of the school's Language of Learning. This is an everyday common focus for pupils and staff which is embedded within the culture of the school.
Our Academics Subjects
Art & Design Technology
Art and Design Technology (DT) is taught to all children by specialist teachers in a custom-built Art and also DT room. The emphasis is on enjoyment and creative problem solving, as well as instilling technical skills, cultural context and historical knowledge. The Department is well-resourced, and learners can work in a wealth of mediums, such as clay, paint, mixed media and computer aided design.
We are proud to deliver a rich and engaging Computing curriculum from Years 1 to 8, underpinned by the nationally recognised Teach Computing framework developed by the National Centre for Computing Education. This carefully structured programme ensures pupils develop both the knowledge and skills to thrive in a digital world, preparing them for further education and future careers in an increasingly technology-driven society.
The Computing curriculum is delivered in line with three key strands: Computer Science, Information Technology, and Digital Literacy. These areas are progressively built upon year after year to ensure a clear progression of skills and knowledge.
In the early years of their Computing journey, students use iPads to explore computing concepts in a hands-on and age-appropriate way. Computing is taught as a discrete subject from year 1 in Pre- Prep. Pupils begin by learning how to stay safe online, understanding the basics of personal information, and how to use digital devices responsibly. They are introduced to coding through block-based programming. Children also learn to use technology for creating and presenting information, including simple data handling, word processing, and multimedia projects.
From Year 5 onwards, pupils transition to using Microsoft Surface devices, allowing for more sophisticated software and a broader range of learning opportunities. These years build on earlier foundations, introducing more advanced programming concepts using Scratch, Python, and web development tools. Students explore computer networks, data representation, and algorithms, while continuing to develop digital literacy skills such as evaluating online sources, collaborative work in cloud environments, and effective use of presentation and spreadsheet tools.
Throughout these years, pupils are encouraged to become creators—not just consumers—of technology. Students gain a deep understanding of how technology works and how it can be used creatively and ethically. We believe that digital competence is essential for success in the modern world, and our approach ensures every child leaves Year 8 with the confidence, curiosity, and capability to navigate and contribute to our digital future.
The English Department has an energetic and forward-looking team who strive to inspire a love of reading and writing in the children. We aim to promote creativity and self-confidence in a positive and caring environment. Throughout there is a clear focus on the development of literacy skills which underpin all work across the curriculum. In both Key Stages 2 and 3, we aim to engender a love and appreciation of literature and an awareness of non-fiction material, and introduce children to a variety of writing styles and writing types.
Our aim is to develop children as independent learners while providing the skills they will need in future life. Lessons are planned to allow the children to participate in a wide variety of learning experiences, with an emphasis on group and independent work, and become effective communicators and active learners.
Geography explains the world we live in. Planet Earth is our home, and the Geography department aims to show young geographers how wonderful, diverse, awesome and yet fragile this home is. Interest in the interaction and interconnectedness between people and the world in which they live will be of value to children in many spheres beyond the classroom, and a love for learning, a respect for difference and an informed concern about the world is encouraged.
Physical and Human Geography are taught in subject-specific lessons from Year 3, with topics ranging from weather and climate to tectonic activity, geomorphology, economic development, and sustainability. Atlases, maps and other textbooks are issued to the children, and their own research is encouraged through these mediums and the use of ICT. Investigations and fieldwork form a vital part of their studies. Children enjoy getting their hands dirty and feet wet, locally and further afield (e.g., in Iceland).
Topics related to the common entrance syllabus are covered in Years 7 and 8, when students can explore issues that are current or of particular interest in more depth. A research project is carried out at the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, building on skills in primary data gathering and analysis. Separate lessons for scholars enable a deeper approach to the subject and more opportunity to focus on developing the skills of responding to and interpreting data, valuable across the curriculum.
The Department aims to create an interactive and dynamic learning environment in which every pupil feels confident to express their ideas while also respecting each other’s opinions, attitudes and beliefs. History at Hilden Grange is intended to be fun but challenging for all the pupils. If a pupil leaves with a genuine fascination and appreciation of the wealth and excitement of this subject, then the Department will have succeeded.
The Ancient Egyptians, Ancient Greeks, Romans, Tudors, Stuarts, Victorians and World War 2 are the key areas of study between Years 3 and 6. The curriculum in Years 7 and 8 will evaluate a wide range of wars, events and people from a variety of historical periods.
At Hilden Grange, pupils begin their study of Latin in Year 7. They are taught to understand the value of the subject and the many ways in which it will support their work in other areas. In the early stages, lessons involve basic vocabulary and identifying Latin roots in English and other languages. By means of word games and other practical activities, pupils soon realise how an understanding of Latin will help them with spelling, grammar and vocabulary, and they begin to develop a greater, more critical awareness of language in general. We dispel the notion that Latin is ‘dead’ but is rather an integral part of other languages and that the legacy of the Romans is everywhere around us in daily life.
Translation work, both from and into Latin, forms a rigorous element of language study and pupils thrive on the challenge that reading short stories presents, while at the same time increasing their grammatical and analytical skills. By the time they reach Year 8, many will be able to read Latin texts at a very high level.
In Classics lessons, language study is put into context as we consider the daily life of Ancient Rome and Roman Britain, including gladiators, slaves, the Roman baths, the army, houses, schools and the geography of the Roman Empire, among other topics. Pupils enjoy project work on Homer’s 'The Odyssey', the Trojan War and Greek Mythology, all of which provide opportunities for creative writing, artwork and performance.
The Maths Department at Hilden Grange aims to instil an enthusiasm and love for Mathematics, creating a happy, organised environment that promotes positive, confident attitudes towards Mathematics. Pupils in the prep school are placed into three groups; these smaller classes allow us to extend and support our children, enabling them to reach their full potential. The Maths staff in the prep school are specialist teachers, ensuring the correct foundations are laid for secondary school and beyond.
Each year the Maths Department participates in the Primary and Junior Maths Challenge as well as competitions organised by local prep schools. We are always very proud of our success at these events. We also run an exciting ‘House Maths Race’ at the end of the summer term.
The study of Modern Languages is flourishing at Hilden Grange. In 2017, Spanish was introduced to the curriculum to be taught in the prep school alongside French and the opportunity to study the two Romance languages has proved very popular.
The emphasis throughout the school years is on communication, ensuring pupils can hold conversations (albeit at different levels) on the topics they study. As early as Reception, children are encouraged to use different languages for simple greetings and to answer the register. French is introduced in Years 1 and 2 through games, songs and other fun activities. This theme continues into the prep school years, when the focus continues to be on communication and confidence building. Pupils engage in role play, pair work and other practical activities so that vocabulary is built through structured topics based on everyday life (e.g., family, friends, home, school, food, shopping).
From Year 5 onwards, written work becomes a more focal point of study. Grammar is taught rigorously and with adequate time spent to ensure thorough consolidation of each topic. The key skills of listening, speaking, reading and writing are equally weighted as is in line with GCSE teaching. Our pupils are therefore very well prepared for entry to senior school, whether this transition be in Year 6 or Year 8.
Educational visits to France or Spain currently take place in the summer term for pupils in Years 7 and 8; venues have previously included Provence, Normandy and Barcelona. These cultural trips offer a wide range of cross-curricular learning opportunities and the chance to speak the language. They also provide lasting, happy memories for pupils of their time at Hilden Grange.
Music is taught to all pupils from Nursery to Year 6 as well as non- scholarship students in year 7 and 8.
In pre-prep, learners have one weekly lesson in which singing, rhythm and percussion are the focus. There is a foundation of Kodaly and Dalcroze pedagogy that underpins all learning. Learners also take part in small ensembles with the Pre-Prep Choir, Ocarinas and Boomwhackers being very popular.
As pupils progress through the years, practical music making, grounded in sound theoretical knowledge develops into skills that leads to purposeful composition, learning about various composers and music from around the world, and developing singing and listening skills. Pupils in year 3 and 4 learn the recorder, combining it with xylophones for pentatonic compositions in the Summer of year 4. In year 5 and 6 there is a focus on keyboard and ukulele skills. Making music with others is a real focus that leads to enjoyment of the subject, and healthy attendance at music ensembles.
Music technology is taught to students from year 4 upwards and in year 7 and 8 gives students an opportunity to become confident with software such as Musescore, which prepares them their music learning journeys at Senior school.
In addition to scheduled lessons, we offer several choral ensembles, including a large choir, the lower prep singing group, Girl Choristers, a Disney choir and an elite group of vocalists in G5, which includes our boy choristers. New initiatives in the next academic year includes the development of a school orchestra. We have a longstanding tradition of supporting boys who are choristers at Tonbridge school.
All ensembles will be entered at the Sevenoaks arts festival.
See Full List of Ensembles
12 visiting teachers provide instrumental lessons and help prepare learners for their music exams as well as concerts within school.
Music threads through school life. There is weekly singing in assemblies, mass singing at the annual Christmas Carol Service, school musical, as well as the Summer Prizegiving not to mention the plethora of end of term assemblies. There are termly solo recitals and ensemble concerts. Music students have an opportunity to shine at the annual Peri Proms that runs in the spring term.
Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education (PSHEE) is taught by form tutors in a dedicated weekly lesson. We teach Jigsaw PSHEE. This mindful, child-centred approach to PSHEE is an original and comprehensive scheme of learning which integrates personal, social, health and economic education with an emphasis on emotional literacy.
Our teaching aims to help children know and value who they really are and how they relate to other people in this ever-changing world.
Religious Studies at Hilden Grange understands that we live in a broadly Christian country, but all six major living religions are studied as well. We consider that it is important for pupil’s social, moral, spiritual and cultural development to be aware of the traditions and history of religion in this country as well as around the world. This builds tolerance and understanding in many areas of life.
In Year 3 and 4, many of the Old and New Testament Bible stories are covered, relating the lessons learned from these to everyday circumstances. In today’s increasingly secular society we consider it important that we provide a literary, cultural and historical background to our studies, by looking closely at the Bible, a book that few are familiar with nowadays. Early Years
A Leading Early Years School in Tonbridge
At our early learning school in Tonbridge, learners are challenged to unleash their full potential in a vibrant, stimulating setting that promotes growth, builds key competencies and cultivates skills in diverse areas.
The early years are a pivotal stage in a child’s school career; we recognise this and provide excellent opportunities for your child to develop their distinct character, gain critical skills for school and later life, and pursue their unique interests. Supported by talented early years specialists, our learners build solid foundations for success at the pre-prep level.
Our early learning school has two stages: Nursery and Reception.
From 5 January 2027, our Nursery will introduce a new 50-week model alongside our existing 35-week term-time option, giving families the flexibility to choose the option that suits them best.
Available to children from the academic term in which they turn three, our extended provision offers flexible attendance and wrap-around care from 7:30 am to 6 pm.
Applications are now open
Why Choose Our Early Years School?
As one of the leading early learning schools in Tonbridge, our goal is to nurture resilient, confident and independent pupils. Our personalised early years programme, led by specialist teachers, covers all the core areas of learning while also catering to learners’ interests and sense of creativity. Parental involvement is encouraged and supported with tools such as Arc Pathway, that allow you to track your child's progress.
Our early years spaces are meticulously planned to promote comfort, calmness, wellbeing and a sense of belonging. Outdoor learning is prioritised at this stage; a custom-built outdoor area and regular Forest School sessions give learners unparalleled opportunities to develop physically and explore the natural world.
An Extended Nursery Day
An Extended Nursery Day
Our Nursery day runs from 8:25 am to 3:20 pm, with Breakfast Club and after-school care extending provision from 7:30 am to 6 pm.
Support During the Holidays
Support During the Holidays
Children enrolled in our 50-week model can continue attending during holiday periods, supported by our expert Nursery team.
Flexible Attendance Options
Flexible Attendance Options
Every teacher in the Inspired group has been hand-selected for their values and commitment to outstanding academic provision. From sports coaches to subject specialists, our staff bring top credentials, blending innovative methods and global best practices to promote excellence, inspire curiosity and instil a lifelong love of learning.
Early Years Curriculum
Our ambitious curriculum is comprised of both child- and teacher-led learning, enriched by topics related to learners’ interests. In accordance with the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework, our lessons are oriented around seven learning areas, including three prime and four specific areas. The prime areas are Communication and Language, Physical Development, and Personal, Social and Emotional Development, while the specific areas include Literacy, Mathematics, Understanding the World, and Expressive Arts and Design.
Communication and Language
There is a strong emphasis on stimulating children’s speaking and listening skills. At our early learning school in Tonbridge, learners develop a love of language in its broadest sense and books in particular. This fosters a rich vocabulary and an understanding of the rhythm and pattern of words in stories and the spoken word. Listening is important not only for instructions, but also for understanding concepts and listening to others' points of view.
Physical Development
Physical activity is vital to children’s all-round development, enabling them to pursue happy, healthy, and active lives. Gross and fine motor skills are developed using a variety of materials and apparatus appropriate to learners' age and ability. Nursery children have one PE session twice a week with the Head of Girls’ Games and one Games lesson with school PE staff. Reception children have one Games lesson with the prep school’s PE staff and one dedicated PE lesson with the Head of Girls’ Games.
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Children are encouraged to develop independence, confidence, sensitivity and respect for other cultures. We also provide opportunities for them to work as part of a group, appreciating others’ efforts and understanding of what is right or wrong by following the ‘Golden Rules’ of the school. At our early learning school in Tonbridge, learners follow the ‘Hidden Garden Pre-Prep’ PSHE curriculum, which runs throughout the pre-prep and beyond.
Literacy
This area focuses on reading and writing. Reading in the early years comprises phonics, language comprehension and word reading. Children are taught to read using the Read, Write, Inc. synthetic phonics programme. Writing involves transcription (spelling and handwriting) and composition (articulating ideas and structuring them in speech).
Mathematics
Developing a strong grounding in numbers is essential to promote fluency in the necessary building blocks that allow children to excel mathematically. The Maths curriculum provides rich opportunities to develop children’s skills in counting, understanding and using numbers, solving simple addition and subtraction problems, and describing shapes, spaces and measurements.
Understanding the World
This area involves guiding children to make sense of their physical environment and community. Children are taken on trips outside the school to increase their awareness of the world around them. They are also exposed to a wealth of stories, non-fiction, rhymes and songs that help strengthen their understanding of our socially, culturally, technologically and ecologically diverse world.
Expressive Arts and Design
Our little ones play with a range of media and materials. We also provide many opportunities for them to share their ideas, thoughts and feelings through art, music, movement, dance, role-play, design and technology.
World-Class Early Years Educators
High-quality teaching provision is a hallmark of the early years. Throughout the Nursery and Reception years, learners make excellent progress due to our passionate, experienced teachers and support staff, who work closely with children and their parents to deliver tailored, effective learning interventions. Learners' wellbeing is our top priority: our highly qualified early years teachers offer a seamless transition into both the Nursery and Reception years to ensure that your little one is happy and comfortable from day one. The children also benefit from specialist teachers in Drama, Music and PE, providing an enriched multi-sensory experience.
Purpose-Built Early Years School Facilities
Our early years classrooms are specifically designed to support personal expression, discovery and exploration. Authentic resources, such as china tea sets, ignite children’s imagination and help to strengthen their communication skills. Our pupils enjoy a bespoke outdoor area that allows for practical learning and activities, such as climbing the tangle logs, visiting the underground Hobbit House, investigating the water pump, creating a magic potion in the mud kitchen or digging for treasure in the sand pit. They also benefit from an adventure playground, outdoor classroom, heated swimming pool, wooden trim trail and extensive grounds for nature walks.
Activities in Our Early Years School
Activities at our Tonbridge Nursery and Reception are designed to be stimulating and give learners a thrilling, personalised start to their education. The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework underpins our curriculum, which combines teacher-led and child-initiated learning, and promotes exploration through open-ended activities. Teaching and activities are meticulously crafted in accordance with the EYFS Early Learning Goals, including Personal, Social and Emotional Development, Communication and Language, and Physical Development.
Early Years Entitlement
We are committed to supporting our families in every way possible and are pleased to confirm our participation in the following Early Years Funding initiatives:
15 hours Universal entitlement for 3 and 4 year olds: All 3 and 4 year old's in the UK are eligible. Enjoy Benefits - Nursery Benefit Scheme: We support this salary sacrifice scheme offered by many employers. Tax free Childcare - We accept childcare vouchers and encourage families to explore the Tax-Free Childcare scheme for eligible costs. More information and eligibility details, please visit the Government website: https://www.gov.uk/tax-free-childcare https://www.gov.uk/help-with-childcare-costs/childcare-vouchers
For more details contact admissions@hildengrange.co.uk
Nursery Fees 2026 - 2027
Discover a world of unlimited opportunities at our early learning school in Tonbridge, and begin your child's journey to success today.

Early Years Funding
Early Years Entitlement
Hilden Grange School is a registered to provider of Free Early Education for 3 and 4 year olds.
Children may join our Nursery as Rising 3s (i.e. from age 2 ½+ starting in the term in which they turn three; subject to key physical milestones being met) and transfer to Reception in the September following their fourth birthday.
All children (from the term following their 3rd birthday until the term of their 5th birthday) are eligible to receive a maximum of 15 hours per week for 38 weeks of the year, regardless of parental income. Parents are only able to claim for the number of full weeks in our academic year as designated by Kent County Council (KCC). Our academic year runs for a maximum of 35 weeks.
Parents must choose a minimum of 5 sessions and these can be at any time during the week. A session is either a morning or an afternoon and our sessions are as follows:
Morning session: 8:30am to 11:30am Afternoon session: 12:30pm to 3:30pm Full day session: 8:30am to 3:30pm
Please see the below table of when a child is eligible for the funding.
A child born in the period
Will become eligible for a free place
1 January to 31 March (inclusive)
The start of Term 5 following their birthday (after April holiday)
1 April to 31 August (inclusive)
The start of Term 1 following their birthday (after Summer holiday)
1 September to 31 December (inclusive)
The start of term 3 following their birthday (after Christmas/New Year holiday)
Additional Information About Our Early Years Entitlement
Our Head of Admissions will make the claim on your behalf for all or part of your 15 hours entitlement based on the completion of a KCC Parental declaration which will be sent to you in advance of the start of term.
Please see our fees page on our school website for the cost of our Nursery sessions.
Parents who do not use their full 15 hours may claim the difference through another registered provider. Eligible children are included in a ‘head count’ which is sent to the Kent Early Years and Childcare Unit. Further information is available from the Childcare Advice Line on 03000 412323.
Parents will receive a termly invoice for fees which are paid to Hilden Grange School by Direct Debit. A credit for the Early Years’ Free Entitlement to a maximum of 15 hours per week is applied to this invoice.
The school reserves the right to withdraw from the scheme at any time and will endeavour to give one term’s notice of its intention.
We also accept payment of Nursery fees via childcare vouchers and the UK Government Tax Free Childcare Scheme; please contact our Finance Department for further details.

Forest School
Expanding Horizons in the Natural World
Children have a full day of Forest School once per term. Led by a qualified practitioner in our dedicated outdoor site, Forest School is a key learning experience that involves cultivating new skills, exploring nature and taking risks in a safe environment. Exposure to nature fosters a sense of responsibility for the environment. Learners become stewards of the natural world as they learn about conservation, sustainability and the importance of caring for the planet. In Forest School, we have three rules: Look after yourself; look after each other; and look after nature.
Explore Our Forest School Site
Benefits of Forest School
Forest School Curriculum
Forest School sessions are a mixture of adult- and child-led activities. Adult-led activities, such as fire lighting, den building, tool use and cooking, are designed to develop key skills, while child-led activities follow learners’ unique interests and are supported by adults where relevant.
Children are introduced to age-appropriate tools (e.g., peelers, drills, knives, saws) that can be used for whittling, woodcraft, and shelter building. By using these tools responsibly, they develop their fine motor skills, problem-solving abilities, and spatial awareness, and learn the importance of safety, patience and risk management.
Our site provides a safe yet challenging space for children to develop their physical abilities. There are many opportunities for ‘risky’ play, such as tree-climbing, balancing on logs and navigating natural obstacles. Activities like these promote physical strength, gross motor skills, resilience and coordination while also encouraging children to assess risk and make decisions independently.
Fires and cooking are key parts of the Forest School experience. Children learn practical skills like fire building and cooking, which promote teamwork, creativity, and an understanding of food preparation.
Discover the outstanding experiences that we offer in the form of a challenging, stimulating and enriching Forest School programme.
